svg.aria-label: A probability axis from zero to one divided into three bands: below a lower threshold the system refuses and says it did not understand, between the two thresholds it asks for a single confirmation, and above the upper threshold it acts on its own. The thresholds shown are illustrative and are meant to be set from your own measurements. A separate panel below states a second rule that overrides the first: an action on a list you marked destructive stops for approval no matter how high the probability, because confidence is a statement about the model and permission is a statement about you.
svg.text: A CALIBRATED PROBABILITY MAKES AUTONOMY A DIAL

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Every decision comes back with a number, so the policy can be written down.

svg.text: Those two thresholds are placeholders. Set them from your own logged decisions, not from this picture.
THE RULE THAT OVERRIDES THE DIAL

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Anything you marked destructive stops for approval at any probability, including 1.00.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Confidence is a statement about the model. Permission is a statement about you.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Collapsing the two is the commonest way an assistant that works becomes an assistant you regret.
